advances: Weighted depth at actual centroid marks for the specified eight-node midpoint pattern, uniformly over its allowable dimensions, translations and radii. There is no general forest aggregation claim.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write the fibers as $a_i+r_iK$ with $K$ of centroid zero, so $a_i$ is the actual centroid and $w_i=|K|_d r_i^d$. The exact edge equalities imply the corresponding midpoint identities of both radii and centroids, by comparing volumes and then taking centroids. Root maximality gives $w_0\le w_2$, $w_5\le w_3$, and $w_7\le w_4$. The last edge implies $r_6=(r_7+r_4)/2\le r_4$, and the preceding edge implies $r_2=2r_4-r_6\ge r_4$. Thus $w_6,w_7\le w_4\le w_2$.

Denote the centroid marks by $q_i=(p_i,a_i)$. At $q_3,q_2$ the own weights guarantee $A,G$, respectively. At $q_1=(q_0+q_2)/2$, any containing halfspace retains at least one of $q_0,q_2$, so its weight is at least $w_1+\min(w_0,w_2)=L$. At $q_4$, the pair $q_3,q_5$ is opposite, and
$$
q_6-q_4=q_4-q_2,\qquad q_7-q_4=2(q_4-q_2).
$$
Thus the second line has $q_6,q_7$ on one ray and $q_2$ on the opposite ray. The sign of a containing halfspace's normal on $q_6-q_4$ ensures it contains either both $q_6,q_7$ or $q_2$; with zero sign it contains all three. The two groups have disjoint indices, and adding the own weight gives the uniform score $w_4+\min(w_3,w_5)+\min(w_2,w_6+w_7)=B+\min(G,C)$. Hence one of the four marks guarantees $D$ in every containing cap.

The root orders give $C\le2w_4\le w_4+w_2\le B+G$. If $C\le G$, the disjoint blocks $A,G,L,B+C$ sum to $T$ and each is at most $D$. If $C>G$, use the blocks $A,L,B+G,C$: the third is at most $D$ by its definition and the fourth by $C\le B+G$. This proves $T\le4D$.

For the selected mark all fibers are full-dimensional, compact and convex, their graph marks are their true centroids, and $0<D\le T$ since each score is bounded by the total of disjoint positive weights. Accepted fact c2180d0c4d7ea592 applies with $\alpha=D$ and gives the claimed lower bound in the actual source, including caps with zero continuous normal.

In the revised interval example with weights $(50,75,100,68,68,68,36,4)$ in hundredth units, the five blocks are $(A,G,L,B,C)=(68,100,125,136,40)$. Thus $D=176>469/4$ in those units. This evaluates a guaranteed score; it is not a claim of exact depth.

statement:
Let $p_0,\ldots,p_7$ in order be $(-1,-2),(-1,-1),(-1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(2,3)$. Let an actual compact convex source in $\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^d$ for an integer $d\ge1$ have these eight positive integer fibers and no others, all translates of positive homothetic copies of a common convex body with nonempty interior. Assume that the volume-maximal parity roots are $2,1,3,4$ in parities $(1,0),(1,1),(0,0),(0,1)$, and that the edges $0\to1,5\to4,6\to4,7\to6$ with respective partners $2,3,2,4$ satisfy exact Minkowski midpoint equalities. Let $w_i$ denote the volume of fiber $i$ and $T=\sum_iw_i$. Give the graph of actual fiber centroids the atomic weights $w_i$. Write
$$
A=w_3,\qquad G=w_2,\qquad L=w_0+w_1,\qquad B=w_4+w_5,\qquad C=w_6+w_7.
$$
One of the marks at indices $3,2,1,4$ has raw atomic depth at least $D=\max\lbrace A,G,L,B+\min(G,C)\rbrace\ge T/4$. The same mark has raw mixed depth at least $\gamma_d D\ge\gamma_d T/4$, where $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Here depth is the infimum of the respective mass over closed ambient halfspaces containing the mark.
